sources.title: Acta Orientalia Academiae Scientiarum Hungaricae — Submissions
sources.note: Official journal submissions page read. It asks for work on the philology, linguistics, literature or history of pre-modern Asia. Asia and the named language/literature subjects come from this stated remit, not from 'Orientalia', 'Scientiarum' or the academy's Hungarian identity.

sources.title: Arabica: Journal of Arabic and Islamic Studies — Instructions for Authors
sources.note: Official Brill author instructions read. The stated scope covers the Arab world's classical and contemporary languages, literatures, history, thought and civilization, welcomes Islamicate studies, and identifies Arabic and Islamic studies in the journal title. The categories record this remit without treating Brill's location as subject geography.

sources.title: Belleten — Aim and Scope
sources.note: Official journal aim-and-scope page read. It focuses on Turkish history and the history of Turkey, and explicitly publishes archaeology, history of art and cultural studies. Turkey is the studied region named by the remit, not merely the publisher's country.

sources.title: Journal of Chinese Overseas — Overview
sources.note: Official Brill overview read. The journal studies Chinese communities and people of Chinese descent throughout the world and explicitly situates that work in diaspora and transnational studies. No East Asia geography is inferred for a worldwide population remit.

sources.title: Monumenta Serica — Journal information
sources.note: Taylor & Francis journal page read. It describes Monumenta Serica as publishing in all fields of Sinology, mainly Chinese culture, and explicitly includes Chinese history, language and literature; adjacent East Asian subjects are included when related to China. East Asia represents the stated study area, not the publisher location.

sources.title: Central Asiatic Journal — Harrassowitz journal description
sources.note: Official publisher description read. It identifies an international periodical for the languages, literature, history and archaeology of Central Asia and describes its focus on the region's linguistic, cultural and historical heritage. Central Asia is the stated study area, not a title-word guess.

sources.title: Asian Perspectives — University of Hawaiʻi Press
sources.note: Official publisher title page read. It calls Asian Perspectives an archaeological journal devoted to the prehistory of Asia and the Pacific and explicitly welcomes archaeology, ethnoarchaeology, physical anthropology and ethnography. Asia Pacific is the stated study area, not the publisher's location.

sources.title: Cahiers d'Études africaines — À propos
sources.note: Cairn journal about page read. It describes an interdisciplinary journal privileging anthropological and historical approaches and covering Africa, the Antilles and the Black Americas. The regional and diaspora categories reflect those named study populations and areas, not the journal's French platform.
